heading.title: Tools
heading.description: Choose what the agent may do on its own and what it must ask you about first.

tools.policyHelp: Automatic lets tools that only look at things run freely and asks before anything that changes something. Off hides the tool from the agent completely.
tools.policyLabel: When the agent wants to use “{{name}}”

lockedReason.shell: Turn on “Allow shell commands” above to use this.
lockedReason.default: Always on. Each tool it reaches is checked on its own.

shellUnrestricted.title: Shell commands run without asking
shellUnrestricted.message: Commands run without asking. The agent can change or delete files and send data out of this computer.

yoloMode.title: Yolo mode is on
yoloMode.message: Every tool runs without asking, including the shell once it is allowed. The agent can also open and act in any app on this computer without asking which ones first. It can change or delete files, run commands, and send data out of this computer on its own.

names.office_edit: Create and edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint files

shell.description: Lets the agent run commands on your computer (Terminal on Mac, PowerShell on Windows).

enable.label: Allow shell commands
enable.description: It asks you before every command unless you choose “Run without asking” in the list below. Commands can change or delete files, so only approve ones you understand.

confirm.title: Run shell commands without asking?
confirm.description: The agent will run every command right away, without showing it to you first. Commands can change or delete files and send data out of this computer. Only turn this on if you trust the agent, the model and the content it reads.

enable.label: Yolo mode
enable.description: Skips the approval step for every tool that is already allowed, including the shell once “Allow shell commands” is on, and the first-use check for apps the “Use apps on this computer” tool opens. It does not turn anything on by itself.

confirm.title: Turn on yolo mode?
confirm.description: The agent will run every allowed tool right away, without asking first, including shell commands once they are allowed, and it can open and act in any app on this computer without asking which ones first. It can change or delete files, run commands, and send data out of this computer. Only turn this on if you trust the agent, the model and the content it reads.

empty.title: No tools yet
empty.description: Tools appear here once the agent has started. Connect business systems in MCP servers.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.description: Pick the search services the agent can use. It tries them in order and moves on to the next when one fails. Keys stay encrypted on this computer. When none of them answers, or none is turned on, the agent uses Exa and DuckDuckGo without a key: your search words are sent to them.
webSearch.summaryEmpty: No search service turned on. Exa and DuckDuckGo are used without a key.
webSearch.loadError: Couldn't load the web search settings.

endpoint.label: {{provider}} server address
endpoint.webclawPlaceholder: Server address (leave empty for webclaw cloud)

key.label: {{provider}} API key
key.saved: Key saved. Type to replace it.

heading.title: Skills
heading.description: Ready-made instructions the agent follows for specific tasks.

empty.title: No skills yet
empty.description: Write your own, or import one someone shared with you (a folder, .zip, or .skill file).

skills.usageHint: The agent picks a matching skill on its own. To use one yourself, type <kbd>/skill:name</kbd> in the chat, for example <kbd>/skill:{{example}}</kbd>.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this skill?
deleteConfirm.description: “{{name}}” and every file in its folder will be removed. This can't be undone.

skillEditor.intro: A skill is a set of instructions the agent follows for a specific kind of task.

validation.nameFormat: Use only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-).
validation.descriptionRequired: Describe what the skill does and when to use it.

name.label: Name
name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Use it in a chat by typing <kbd>/skill:{{name}}</kbd>.

description.label: Description
description.placeholder: Summarises a weekly sales export by region and product. Use when someone asks for a sales summary or weekly numbers.
description.hint: Say what it does and when to use it. The agent reads this to decide when the skill fits. {{current}}/{{max}}

auto.label: Let the agent use this automatically
auto.description: When off, the skill only runs when someone types /skill:{{name}}.

body.label: Instructions
body.placeholder:
# Weekly sales summary

1. Read the sales export the person points to.
2. Group the totals by region and by product.
3. Write a short summary with the three biggest changes since last week.
body.hint: Step-by-step instructions for the agent, written in Markdown.

files.label: Other files in this skill
files.hint: The agent can open these when it follows the instructions. Change them in the skill folder.

heading.title: MCP servers
heading.description: Connect the agent to business systems such as a CRM, ticketing, or a database.

mcp.checking: Checking connections… this can take a few seconds.
mcp.configErrors: Some servers in mcp.json couldn't be loaded

empty.title: No servers yet
empty.description: MCP servers give the agent tools for your business systems. Add one with the details from its setup guide, or paste a configuration from Claude Desktop or Cursor.

signOutConfirm.title: Sign out of “{{name}}”?
signOutConfirm.description: The agent won't be able to use this server until you sign in again.

removeConfirm.title: Remove this server?
removeConfirm.description: “{{name}}” and its tools will no longer be available to the agent.

connectors.description: Connect the agent to the apps you work in, so it can look things up and make changes there for you.
connectors.googleRefused: Google refused access. In the app's Google Cloud project, enable both the product's API (for example Gmail API) and its MCP API (Gmail MCP API), and check that this account is a test user.

addAccount.title: Add another {{name}} account
addAccount.description: Give it a short name so you and the agent can tell your accounts apart.
addAccount.label: Account name

address.title: {{name}} address
address.description: Enter your company's hub address — the one you open in the browser.
address.label: Hub address
address.invalid: Use an https address such as {{example}}.

gmail.description: Search and read your email, and write drafts for you to send.

calendar.description: See your events and when you are free.

drive.description: Find and read files in Google Drive, and save new ones.

docs.description: Read and edit documents in Google Docs.

sheets.description: Read and edit spreadsheets in Google Sheets.

notion.description: Search and edit pages and databases in your Notion workspace.

linear.description: Find, create and update Linear issues, projects and comments.

atlassian.description: Work with Jira issues and Confluence pages.

sentry.description: Look into errors and performance problems in Sentry.

stripe.description: Look up customers, payments, invoices and subscriptions in Stripe.

supabase.description: Query and manage your Supabase projects and databases.

context7.description: Up-to-date documentation and code examples for programming libraries.

pp-hub.description: Your company drive: find, read, create and edit documents, share them and comment.

filesystem.description: Read and change files inside one folder on this computer.

email.cardDescription: Read, search, send and file email in your own mailbox over IMAP and SMTP. The password is kept in secure storage on this computer.
email.intro: Your password for this mailbox. Most providers need an app password instead of your account password.

address.label: Email address
address.hint: The address mail is read from and sent as.

label.label: Name (optional)
label.hint: Shown in this list and to the agent, when the mailbox is not the only one.

displayName.label: Display name (optional)
displayName.hint: The name recipients see on your messages.

password.label: Password or app password
password.keep: Leave empty to keep the saved password
password.hint: Kept in the computer's secure storage, never in a settings file.

secure.imapHint: On for port 993; off for 143, which upgrades with STARTTLS.
secure.smtpHint: On for port 465; off for 587, which upgrades with STARTTLS.

servers.description: Filled in from the provider; change them only if your company runs its own mail server.
servers.note: Use the servers your mail administrator gave you. The sign-in name is the address unless the server needs another.

validation.address: Enter the email address of this mailbox.
validation.port: The ports must be numbers between 1 and 65535.

removeConfirm.title: Remove this mailbox?
removeConfirm.description: “{{name}}” and its saved password will be removed. The agent can no longer read or send from it.

mcpJson.hint: You can paste a configuration from Claude Desktop or Cursor here: the servers inside its "mcpServers" block work as they are.
mcpJson.intro: The file that lists your MCP servers. For advanced setups.

mcpForm.intro: Copy these details from the server's setup guide, or ask your tech team.

validation.nameFormat: Use only letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
validation.nameTaken: Another server already uses this name.
validation.urlInvalid: Enter a web address starting with https:// or http://.
validation.timeoutInvalid: Enter a number of seconds, or leave it empty.

name.label: Name
name.hint: A short name, shown next to the server's tools. Letters, digits, _ and -.

description.label: Description (optional)
description.hint: Helps the agent understand what this server is for.

command.label: Command
command.hint: The program that starts the server on this computer.

env.label: Environment variables
env.hint: Settings the server reads when it starts, such as access tokens.

url.label: Server URL
url.hint: If the server needs you to sign in, leave the headers empty and use “Sign in” after saving.

headers.label: Headers
headers.hint: Sent with every request, for example an API key.

exposure.label: How the agent sees its tools

timeout.label: Time limit per request (seconds)
timeout.hint: Leave empty unless the server is slow to answer.

trusted.label: Trust this server's read-only labels
trusted.description: Tools the server marks as read-only then run without asking. Leave off unless you trust who runs the server: otherwise every tool asks first.

codemode.label: Through scripts (recommended)
codemode.description: The agent combines this server's tools in small scripts. Works well even with many tools.

deferred.label: On demand
deferred.description: The agent looks up this server's tools when it needs them.

direct.label: Always available
direct.description: Every tool is offered to the agent all the time. Best for servers with few tools.

hidden.label: Hidden
hidden.description: The server stays connected, but the agent can't see its tools.
